explanation: This is safe. Both inc() and get() are synchronized on the same monitor, so a reader can never observe a torn or intermediate value, and the synchronized-acquire releases establish happens-before — no stale-read race exists. A tempting wrong answer assumes reads need to be volatile, but synchronized reads that lock the same monitor the writer uses are sufficient here.
prompt: Two threads call inc() while a third reads get(). Is the value ever stale or torn?
left_label: Race — get() reads a stale value
